# check-pr — one tending pass over a set of pull requests

Usage:

```text
/skill:craft-check-pr [<pr> ...] [--fix auto|ask]
```

- `<pr>` is a bare number (`123`) for the current repo, or a full PR
  URL for any repo. Several may be given. With none, use the PR for the
  branch checked out in the current directory (`gh pr view`).
- `--fix ask` (default): for a comment worth fixing, reply with the
  proposed change and wait for approval before touching code.
- `--fix auto`: for a comment worth fixing, make the change, push, and
  reply with what changed.

Every run is one pass. It reads all of its state from GitHub and from
git, keeps no files of its own, and ends with one report line per PR.
That is what makes it safe to call from a loop: a tick that finds
nothing new does nothing and says so. The one thing it writes besides
replies and commits is the answer to a finding of `/skill:craft-review-pr`
(step 5), recorded on that PR's state ref.

Work only on the PR's head branch, in its own worktree, never in the
main checkout. Never force-push without `--force-with-lease`. Never
merge, close, or approve a PR. If the repo has a CLAUDE.md or
CONTRIBUTING file, its commit and branch rules apply to every commit
this skill makes.

# Agent work identity

At the start of each pass, record one identity for the work the pass performs.
Use it unchanged in every review, comment, response, marker, and final report
from that pass.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Actor | The authenticated GitHub login from `gh api user --jq .login` |
| Agent | The harness running the pass (`Codex` or `Claude`) |
| Model | The exact model id the agent runs as, read from its own system prompt (for example `claude-opus-4-1`), never a family name such as `opus`; `unknown` only when it is not exposed |
| Effort | The reported reasoning effort, or `unknown` |
| Host | `hostname` |
| Session | `<host>:<harness>-<6 random chars>` (for example `mbp:claude-k3x9qa`), generated once at the start of the pass and reused unchanged. Use `<host>:<pid>` instead only when the harness itself exposes its process id; never a shell's `$$` or `$PPID` |
| Skill | `<skill-name>@<plugin-version>` from the host's plugin manifest; `<skill-name>@dev` when there is no manifest (a development tree); `<skill-name>@unknown` only when a manifest exists but has no version |
| Started | `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` at the start of the pass |

Do not guess a value the harness does not expose. Write `unknown` instead; the random session
suffix above is the one value you generate yourself. Values placed in an HTML marker must contain no
spaces; use `unknown` when a value cannot be represented that way.

## Comment signature

Append this short, visible signature to every inline finding posted by
`/skill:craft-review-pr` and every response posted by `/skill:craft-check-pr`:

```markdown
<sub>🤖 <agent> · <model> · <skill></sub>
```

Follow it with this hidden, machine-readable record:

```html
<!-- pr-tools: actor=<actor> agent=<agent> model=<model> effort=<effort> session=<session> skill=<skill> at=<started> -->
```

`/skill:craft-check-pr` keeps its existing `<!-- check-pr: re=<comment-databaseId> -->`
marker on top-level responses. Add the `pr-tools` record as a separate marker;
the reply marker remains the source of truth for duplicate detection.

## Remote for the state script

`review-state.mjs` writes to a git remote. Decide once per PR whether it belongs to the repository
the checkout's `origin` points at: normalise `origin`'s URL to `owner/repo` and compare it,
case-insensitively, with the PR's `owner/repo`.

```sh
git remote get-url origin | sed -E 's#^(git@|ssh://([^@/]+@)?|https?://([^@/]+@)?)github\.com[:/]##; s#(\.git)?/?$##'
```

It handles `git@github.com:o/r.git`, `https://github.com/o/r(.git)`, `ssh://git@github.com/o/r` and
URLs carrying `user[:token]@`. When they match, omit `--remote`. For a PR in any other repository,
add `--remote https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git` to every call; it takes a URL as well as a
remote name, and works from a directory that is not a git repository. A GitHub Enterprise or other
non-`github.com` host does not normalise: always pass an explicit `--remote <url>` there.

Pass a PR's commit as the full 40-character sha everywhere a sha is recorded (`fixed in <sha>`,
`--fixed-in`, `--head`, `--base`).

## 1. Resolve the PRs

For each argument, fetch one snapshot:

```sh
gh pr view <pr> -R <owner>/<repo> --json number,url,title,state,isDraft,author,headRefName,baseRefName,headRepositoryOwner,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,comments,reviews,body
```

Check `body` for a lease footer, an HTML comment on the last line such
as `<!-- <tool>-lease: task=<id> lease=<id> -->`, planted by another
tool that owns the PR's lifecycle. A PR carrying one is under that
tool's lease: this skill has no lease coordination, so touching it
directly (rebase, push, or a comment reply) risks racing the owning
tool or corrupting its phase state. Skip rebase and comment handling
for that PR — report its state only, and say in the report that it is
lease-managed and should go through the tool that owns the lease.

Every `gh` call that takes a PR passes the PR's repository (`-R <owner>/<repo>`, or the full PR
URL in place of the number), because the working directory may be a clone of another repository and
a bare number resolves against it. `gh api` paths already carry `<owner>/<repo>`.

Also fetch the review threads, which `gh pr view` does not expose:

```sh
gh api graphql -f query='query($owner:String!,$repo:String!,$n:Int!,$endCursor:String){
  repository(owner:$owner,name:$repo){ pullRequest(number:$n){
    reviewThreads(first:100,after:$endCursor){ pageInfo{ hasNextPage endCursor } nodes{ id isResolved isOutdated
      comments(first:50){ pageInfo{ hasNextPage } nodes{ id databaseId url body author{login} createdAt path line } } } } } } }' \
  --paginate -f owner=<owner> -f repo=<repo> -F n=<number>
```

`--paginate` follows `endCursor` through every page of threads. A thread whose
`comments.pageInfo.hasNextPage` is true has more than 50 comments; fetch the rest of that thread
with a follow-up query on its node `id` before judging whether it is handled.

Record who "we" are once per run: `gh api user --jq .login`. A comment
by that login is ours. Record the rest of the shared identity at the same
time so every response in this pass carries the same comment signature.

A PR whose `state` is `MERGED` or `CLOSED` gets a report line and no
other work. A PR from a fork (`headRepositoryOwner` is not the base
repo's owner) gets comment handling but no rebase, since its branch
cannot be pushed; say so in the report.

## 2. Bring the branch up to date

Decide whether the branch needs a rebase:

- `mergeable == "CONFLICTING"` or `mergeStateStatus == "DIRTY"`: it
  conflicts with its base.
- Otherwise, after `git fetch origin`, count with
  `git rev-list --left-right --count origin/<base>...origin/<head>`.
  A non-zero left count means the branch is behind.

Skip this step when neither holds; step 5 creates the worktree then if it needs one to fix code.
Otherwise:

1. Check out the head branch in a worktree. Reuse
   `<repo-root>/.worktrees/<head>` if it exists, else
   `git worktree add <repo-root>/.worktrees/<head> <head>`. If the repo
   has its own worktree convention, use that location instead.
2. `git rebase origin/<base>`. Rebase, not merge: the PR history stays
   linear and the reviewer's diff stays honest.
3. On conflicts, resolve them only when the intent of both sides is
   clear from the diff and the surrounding code. When it is not,
   `git rebase --abort`, leave the branch as it was, and report the
   conflicting paths. A wrong resolution costs more than a wait.
4. Run the repo's quick checks for the touched area (typecheck, lint,
   the nearest tests). A rebase that breaks them is aborted and
   reported, not pushed.
5. `git push --force-with-lease origin <head>`.

## 3. Find the comments that need a response

Gather the review threads and the top-level PR comments. Ignore any comment we wrote, except the
first comment of a finding thread (below), which is the reviewer's ask even when our login posted
it, because `/skill:craft-review-pr` usually posts as the same login. For each remaining item, decide whether
it is already handled:

- A review thread is handled when it is resolved, or when its last
  comment is ours and no approval is pending on it (see step 5).
- A top-level comment is handled when one of our later comments carries
  the marker `<!-- check-pr: re=<comment-databaseId> -->`. Every reply
  this skill posts to a top-level comment includes that marker, which
  is how the next pass knows it was answered.

Everything else is new and gets an assessment.

A review thread whose first comment carries
`<!-- review-pr: finding=<id> -->` is a finding of `/skill:craft-review-pr`, whoever
posted it. Its `<id>` (such as `r2-1`) names the finding in that PR's
state ref. The first comment is the ask, so the rule "its last comment
is ours" does not apply to it. Such a thread is handled when it is
resolved, or when our latest reply says `fixed in <sha>` or
`declined: <reason>`, which step 5 writes. If our latest reply is a
`--fix ask` proposal and nothing came after it, the thread is pending
as in step 5. Otherwise it is new. Comments without the marker are
handled exactly as before.

## 4. Assess each new comment

Read the comment, the code it points at, and enough of the PR to judge
it. Sort it into one bucket:

- **fix**: a real defect, a correctness gap, or a change the reviewer
  is right to ask for and that fits the PR's scope.
- **decline**: a request that is wrong, out of scope for this PR, or
  costs more than it returns. Say why in one or two sentences and, when
  it belongs elsewhere, say where.
- **answer**: a question. Answer it. No code changes.
- **ack**: a nit or note that needs no action. A one-line reply.

Be honest in the assessment. A reviewer's suggestion is not a fix just
because a reviewer made it, and a defect is not out of scope because it
is inconvenient.

## 5. Respond

Reply in place: on a review thread, use the thread's reply endpoint;
on a top-level comment, post a new PR comment that carries the marker
from step 3. Append the shared short comment signature and its `pr-tools`
marker to every response, including proposals and replies after a fix.

```sh
gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>/comments/<databaseId>/replies -f body='...'
gh pr comment <n> -R <owner>/<repo> --body '...'
```

A top-level response therefore ends with both markers, in this order:

```html
<!-- check-pr: re=<comment-databaseId> -->
<!-- pr-tools: actor=<actor> agent=<agent> model=<model> effort=<effort> session=<session> skill=<skill> at=<started> -->
```

Keep replies short and specific. Name the file and the change, not the
reasoning process.

**Findings of review-pr.** The state script writes to a git remote; the shared instruction above
says when to add `--remote <url>` to every call below.
For a thread with a finding marker, the
reply on the thread and the state ref say the same thing, and both are
written. The state script lives in the sibling `review-pr` skill folder,
`../review-pr/review-state.mjs` relative to this file; where skill
folders carry a plugin prefix (`craft-check-pr`, `craft-review-pr`) it
is the sibling folder whose name ends in `review-pr`. Call it as
`node <review-pr-dir>/review-state.mjs`. If the script cannot be found,
reply on the thread anyway and say in the report that the state ref was
not updated.

- Fixed: reply `fixed in <full 40-character sha>` on the thread, with what changed after it, then
  `node <review-pr-dir>/review-state.mjs answer <pr> --id <id> --status fixed --fixed-in <full sha>`.
- Declined: reply `declined: <reason>` on the thread, the reply beginning with exactly that word,
  then
  `node <review-pr-dir>/review-state.mjs answer <pr> --id <id> --status declined --reason '<reason>'`,
  the reason in single quotes with each `'` inside it written as `'\''`.

The reply text matters: a later review-pr pass rebuilds the state from
these replies when the ref is missing. A failing
`answer` never stops the pass: the thread reply is already posted and a
later review-pr pass rebuilds the state from it. Report the failure
(exit 1: an unknown id, a corrupt or unreachable ref; exit 3: a lost
race after a retry) and carry on. Answers and acknowledgements need no state write.
With `--fix ask`, write the state only when the fix is applied, not
when it is proposed.

Per finding the order is reply, then `answer`, then (for a fix under `--fix auto`) resolve the
thread.

**decline / answer / ack**: post the reply. Do not resolve the thread;
resolving is the reviewer's call.

**fix, with `--fix auto`**: make the change on the head branch in a worktree (create it as in step 2
when that step was skipped), run the quick checks, commit, push, then reply with what changed and
the full commit SHA. Resolve the thread with `resolveReviewThread` in GraphQL, since the reviewer's
ask is met. One commit per PR per pass is fine when several comments are fixed together; list each
comment's URL in the commit body.

**fix, with `--fix ask`**: post the proposed change, concrete enough to
review (the file, the approach, and a short diff sketch when it helps),
ending with the line:

```text
React 👍 to this comment to apply it.
```

Then leave it. On a later pass, a proposal is approved when someone
other than us has given it a `+1` reaction, or has replied in the same
thread agreeing (yes, go ahead, do it, lgtm). Check reactions with:

```sh
gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/comments/<databaseId>/reactions
gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/comments/<databaseId>/reactions
```

An approved proposal is applied exactly as `--fix auto` would apply
it. A reply that pushes back is a new comment: assess it again from
step 4. A proposal with neither is pending; count it in the report and
move on.

## 6. Report

Finish with one line per PR, in this shape, so a loop can read it
without parsing prose:

```text
[#123](<url>) STATE=<open|draft|merged|closed> REBASE=<none|done|conflict|blocked|deferred> CHECKS=<pass|fail|none> COMMENTS=new:<n> replied:<n> fixed:<n> pending:<n>
```

- `REBASE=conflict` means the rebase was aborted on conflicts; list the
  paths below the line. `blocked` means the branch could not be pushed
  (a fork, or a check failure after rebase). `deferred` means step 1
  found a lease footer — no rebase or comment work was
  attempted; `COMMENTS` reads all-zero and the line below names the
  tool that owns the lease.
- `CHECKS` reads `statusCheckRollup`: `fail` when any check concluded
  `FAILURE`, `TIMED_OUT`, `CANCELLED`, or `STARTUP_FAILURE`. A repository with no checks reads
  `none`; say in the report that none were found, and do not invent or run checks to fill the gap.
- `pending` is the number of `--fix ask` proposals still waiting for a
  thumbs-up.

Below the lines, add at most a few sentences on anything a person must
decide: an unresolved conflict, a declined request that the reviewer
may want to escalate, or a failing check the PR did not cause. When
nothing needs a person, say so in one line.
